title: Noa Lang avoids ‘complete thumb amputation’ after Anfield hoardings collision – club doctor
content:
Noa Lang has avoided his thumb being amputated after cutting his hand during a collision with the advertising hoardings at Anfield, Galatasaray’s club doctor has confirmed.

Lang, 26, underwent surgery in Liverpool after sustaining the injury to his right thumb during his side’s Champions League tie against Arne Slot’s side on March 18.

Lang slid into the advertising boards in the latter stages of Galatasaray’s Champions League last-16 loss at Liverpool and had to be taken off on a stretcher after a six-minute delay. He was in visible pain as he left the pitch and the tip of his thumb appeared partially severed.

The incident is the subject of a UEFA investigation and Liverpool confirmed the club would also investigate the incident.

The winger has joined the Netherlands squad for March’s international break, and Galatasaray doctor Yener Ince said he would not be available for the friendly against Norway on Friday, but may feature against Ecuador four days later.

“I want to clarify that there is no complete amputation; however, the injury is significant,” a statement from Ince read.

“Currently, there appear to be no problems, but the Galatasaray medical team is monitoring him. We are in close contact with the Dutch national team’s medical staff.”

The Netherlands international was pictured with a large bandage around his thumb as he took part in national team training on Tuesday.

He confirmed his thumb had been saved and explained that, due to being right-handed, the injury meant he was still struggling with day-to-day activities.

“I still have it (my thumb) completely, that’s the most important thing,” Lang said in an interview with Dutch outlet Ziggo Sport. “I just can’t play PlayStation for a while, but that will come.

“Luckily, I only need my legs to be able to play football.

“I’m right-handed. So that’s not unimportant in the toilet… Things like that, just with showering and stuff, I’m getting a bit of help.”
